Tiramisu cinnamon rolls, la combinación mas fabulosa. ¡Seguro estos roles serán tus nuevos favoritos! ☕️🤍 #cocinaconricardo 
—
Lo que necesitas:
● Ingredientes roles:
○ 240 ml de leche entera (tibia)
○ 2 1/2 cucharaditas de levadura instantánea
○ 2 huevos
○ 90 g de mantequilla salada (derretida)
○ 100 g de azúcar blanco
○ 500 g de harina
○ 1 cucharadita de pasta de vainilla
● Procedimiento roles:
○ En un bowl de batidora agrega leche, una pizca de azúcar y encima levadura. Permite que la levadura active. Agrega huevos, vainilla, mantequilla y azúcar, combina. Agrega harina y mezcla hasta que todo esté a penas incorporado. Deja reposar 5 minutos.
○ Con el gancho, amasa por 5-7 min. La masa debe quedar suave y un poco pegajosa.
○ Transfiere a un bowl engrasado, cubre con plástico y deja reposar mínimo 2 hrs en un lugar tibio.
● Ingredientes base:
○ 113 g de mantequilla (temp. ambiente)
○ 100 g de azúcar mascabado
○ 50 g de azúcar blanco (refinado)
○ 30 g de crema para batir
○ 1 cucharadita de extracto de vainilla
○ 1/4 cucharadita de sal
● Procedimiento base:
○ Mezcla todo y coloca en la base del recipiente de tu elección.
● Ingredientes relleno:
○ 100 g de mantequilla (temp. ambiente)
○ 100 g de azúcar mascabado
○ 1 cucharada de cocoa en polvo
○ 1/2 cucharada (si te gusta mucho el café, 1 cucharada) de café molido espresso
○ 1 cucharadita de canela
○ 1/4 cucharadita de sal
● Procedimiento relleno:
○ Precalienta el horno a 180 C.
○ Con ayuda de una batidora, mezcla todos los ingredientes muy bien.
○ Extiende la masa. Cubre con el relleno. Corta, enrolla y coloca en el recipiente.
○ Hornea por 22-30 minutos.
● Ingredientes glaseado:
○ 225 g de queso mascarpone
○ 60 g de crema para batir.
○ 2 cucharadas de azúcar blanco
○ 1 cucharadita de extracto de vainilla
○ Cocoa en polvo (para decorar)
● Procedimiento glaseado:
○ Combina todo. Coloca sobre roles, y decora con cocoa. ¡Disfruta!
.
.
.

input.transcript: La combinación más fabulosa, tiramisu cinnamon rolls,  que pudiera ser más perfecto que tomar dos postres icónicos  y mezclarlos para obtener un resultado verdaderamente delicioso.  Por un lado tenemos la esperada suavidad del rod de canela  y por otro lado tenemos los contundentes sabores de un tiramisu tradicional.  En este caso, uno de los ingredientes más importantes es el café,  pues además del más carpone el café es el ingrediente que más marca la pauta de sabor,  así que es importante utilizar un café molido de alte calidad.  Saben que una de mis cosas favoritas de cocinar es mezclar culturas,  sabores, ideas y descubrir nuevos postres.  Está ha sido una de mis combinaciones favoritas hasta ahora  y estoy seguro que les va a encantar tanto como a mí.  Qué fabuloso.

input.caption:
Mi flan cremoso de pumpkin spice es uno de esos postres que simplemente definen toda una temporada. Y este podría ser el más bello y reconfortante de todos. Creado utilizando los productos de @califiafarms🌱🤍 #cocinaconricardo 
—
Lo que necesitas:
● Ingredientes caramelo:
○ 150 g de azúcar (blanco, granulado)
● Procedimiento caramelo:
○ En un sartén agrega el azúcar. Permite que todo el azúcar se derrita a fuego muy bajo. Una vez que tenga un bello color y todos los cristales de azúcar se hayan disuelto, retira del fuego.
○ Mezcla delicadamente con un miserable de silicona y vierte el caramelo en el molde de tu elección. Permite que endurezca y enfríe.
● Ingredientes flan (puedes duplicar la receta para obtener un flan con la altura que muestro en el video):
○ 6 huevos
○ 150 ml de unsweetened almondmilk @califiafarms 
○ 100 ml de french vanilla creamer @califiafarms
○ 250 ml de leche condensada
○ 100 ml de crema para batir
○ 125 g de queso crema
○ 1 cucharada de pumpkin spice (2 cucharaditas de canela molida, 1 cucharadita de jengibre molido, 3/4 cucharadita de nuez moscada molida y 1/4 cucharadita de pimienta dulce molida)
○ 1 cucharadita de pasta de vainilla
● Procedimiento flan:
○ Agrega todos los ingredientes en una licuadora. Licúa hasta obtener una mezcla integrada y tersa.
○ Coloca un colador sobre el molde con el caramelo, y vacía la mezcla hacia el molde, pasando por el colador. Tapa.
○ A mi me gusta hacer el flan en vaporera o double boiler (como en el video), pero lo puedes llevar al horno poniendo el molde en una bandeja alta con agua hirviendo. En ambas opciones el tiempo de cocción es de aproximadamente 40-50 minutos (1 hora 50 minutos si duplicas la receta) hasta que cuaje.
○ Una vez pasado el tiempo, retira de la vaporera/horno y permite que enfríe a la intemperie hasta enfriar. Por último, lleva al refrigerador y que repose toda la noche.
○ Al día siguiente, pasa un cuchillo por las orillas y desmolda. Decora y ¡disfruta!
input.transcript: ¿Alguna vez habías visto un flan como este?  Pues este es mi Pumpkin Spice Flan, suave, sedoso y con una mezcla de especias que hace que toda la casa huele increíble.  También es perfecto para sentir que vive en el mundo Gilmore Girls esta temporada.  Y para hacerlo aún mejor estoy usando Califia Almond Milk sin endulzar y un poco de su deliciosos French vanilla creamer  que además de ser a base de plantas nos ayudan a elevar cada receta gracias a que son ingredientes de calidad.  Porque hay postres que simplemente definen toda una temporada y este podría ser el más bello y recomfortante posible  para cuando las hojas empiezan a cambiar de color.  ¿Qué fabuloso?

input.caption: 🤤 New Thai restaurant with TWELVE kinds of Pad Thai 🍜📍Bobo Thai @bobothaiusa #la #restaurant #recommendation #thaifood #noodles
input.transcript: This new Thai restaurant has 12 kinds of pad Thai.  It's actually the first restaurant in LA dedicated to pad Thai.  And as an Asian who eats more noodles than rice, I had to try it out.  First one I got was their classic, the 1938.  After the year Thailand named it their national dish.  I'm picking with pad Thai because it can sometimes taste super ketchupy.  But I didn't get that at all from this.  You'll be happy to know these are not tomato bites.  And in no key mushrooms on the topping, they're so satisfying to eat.  The second one I got is their two kings.  The flavor is just like a Tom Yum soup.  Very bright and citrusy and comes with tofu.  You can add toppings to any of them.  I got shrimp because tofu alone wasn't going to cut it.  Let's be real.  I can't lose further side dishes.  The pork jowl comes with sauce and a lettuce to wrap it in.  And I got broccoli to be healthy, I guess.  My next noodle was their happy place and is a pad cu.  I had a soft shell crab as the topping.  I always get pad cu at Thai restaurants and I'm still most partial to this one.  But the 2AM is a very close second.  It's a similar noodle dish but a lot spicier.  They have rice bowls too that they can't under the pad Thai umbrella.  I love how the Thai cook eggs.  They're the best.  And they came with Thai basil chicken.  Try the map they're called Bobo Thai.

input.caption: fall drinks are here! I tried every single drink at @essntlcoffeesd and I’m so impressed #sandiego #coffee #falldrinks #sandiegocoffee
input.transcript: Essential coffee in San Diego just dropped their fall drinks. They're in the college area and they're known for their Vietnamese coffee matcha and cream top drinks.  They have three different cream tops for their fall series. They have a brown sugar miso, a pumpkin pie cream, and a fig cream.  And you can get each one with either coffee or matcha. So obviously we tried both. The brown sugar miso was probably my favorite.  It was sweet and salty like the perfect balance and I thought it went really well with both the matcha and the coffee.  But the other two were also amazing. The pumpkin pie cream had so much pumpkin spice flavor and was just like fall in a drink.  And then the fig cream was super smooth and very lightly sweet which I really appreciated.  I just love that the drinks feel super fall without just being the exact same fall drinks. You see at every single coffee shop.  So if you're ready for some early fall drinks even though it's literally 90 degrees outside, this is definitely the place to go.

input.caption:
EASY MEALS FOR 2, EP. 15
Creamy Lemon Garlic Scallop Pasta
Ingredients
* 345g Hokkaido scallops
* Salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
* Oil, for searing
* 1 small shallot (about 42g), finely diced
* 4 cloves garlic (about 13g), minced
* ¼ cup water (optional for deglazing)
* ¼ cup water mixed with 1 tsp Hondashi
* ¾ cup heavy cream
* 150g pasta of choice
* ¼ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (plus more to taste)
* Juice of ½ lemon
* Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

Instructions
1. Cook the pasta
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta until 1 minute before al dente. Reserve pasta water
2. Prepare the scallops
Pat the scallops completely dry with paper towels. Season both sides lightly with salt and freshly cracked black pepper.
3. Sear the scallops
Heat a large pan over medium high heat, for the best sear, use a cast iron or stainless steel skillet, I didn't have one so I'm using a nonstick pan, the scallops still came out tasty ! Add a drizzle of oil.
Once the pan is hot, place the scallops in the skillet without overcrowding.
Sear for approximately 2 minutes per side, depending on their size, until a deep golden crust forms. Be careful not to overcook them or they’ll become rubbery.
Transfer the scallops to a plate and set aside.
4. Make the sauce
Reduce the heat to medium.
If needed, deglaze the pan with a splash of water, scraping up any browned bits.
Add:
* diced shallot
* minced garlic
Cook until softened and fragrant, about 1–2 minutes.
Pour in:
* ¾ cup heavy cream
* ¼ cup water mixed with 1 teaspoon Hondashi
Bring to a gentle simmer.
5. Finish the sauce
Stir in the grated Parmesan until melted and smooth.
Add the juice of ½ a lemon.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional Parmesan, salt ( go easy on salt if you're adding in salty pasta water later ), pepper, or lemon juice as needed.
Add the cooked pasta to the sauce along with a splash of reserved pasta water.
Toss until the pasta is evenly coated in the creamy sauce. 
#pasta #scallop #cooking #seafoodpasta #dinnerideas

input.caption:
scallion pancake quesadilla stuffed w/ kungpao chicken 🤤🤤

ingredients: 
chicken breast 
sichuan peppercorn
dried chilis
scallions
garlic
peanuts 
cooking wine
Corn starch
scallion pancake
@tillamook mozzarella 
sauce: 
soy sauce 
dark soy sauce 
black vinegar 
honey

recipe: 
1) cube chicken breast and marinate w/ cooking wine & soy sauce & cornstarch (15 mins) 
2) sauté peppercorn and dried chili in oil and remove
3) add chicken into the oil and cook until it’s 75% done
4) add scallions and garlic and pre-made sauce and cook for another 3-5 mins 
5) add back in chilis and add in the peanuts
6) cook 2 scallion pancakes, add cheese on top of one
7) put chicken on top of the pancake and cheese & press the other pancake on & let it get crispy / melty 

#scallionpancake #chinesefood #latenightcravings #scallionpancakequesadilla #kungpaochicken

👉 Ingredientes:
Base:
Galletitas de vainilla o chocolate 300g
Manteca 150g
Relleno:
Queso crema 900g
Azúcar 200g
4 Huevos
Vainillas 1 paquete
Café fuerte (puede ser con licor también 😎)
Crema de leche 400cc (opcional, es para ponerle por encima de la torta)
cacao amargo c/n 
extracto de vainilla 1 cdta 
almidón de maíz 2 cdas

Paso a paso:
Procesar las galletitas y unir con la manteca derretida. Cubrir la base de un molde desmontable de 24cm.
Relleno: mezclar el queso crema con los huevos, el azúcar, extracto de vainilla y el almidón de maíz.
Colocar una capa sobre la torta.
Por encima colocar las vainillas previamente embebidas en café. Terminar de cubrir con la crema de queso y llevar al horno 170grados a baño maría por 1 hora.
Dejar enfriar y por arriba pueden batir crema a punto chantilly y ponerle encima o simplemente espolvorear xon cacao.  #cheesecake #tiramisú #recetas #pastry #foodie

input.caption:
Brown Butter Cinnamon Roll Focaccia 🤎

• 500g bread flour or all-purpose flour
• 400g warm water
• 7g instant yeast
• 12g sugar or honey
• 20g salt
• 45g olive oil (plus more for the pan if making a savory focaccia)

1. Mix water, yeast, sugar/honey, salt and olive oil. Add flour and mix until no dry spots remain. The dough will be STICKY!
2. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
3. Wet your hands and do 4 sets of stretch and folds, resting 30-45 minutes between each set.
4. Bulk rise 2-4 hours, until doubled, jiggly and bubbly.
5. Generously rub a 9x13 baking dish with butter (for the cinnamon roll focaccia). Pour in the dough and gently stretch toward the edges.
6. Preheat oven to 375. Add the cinnamon topping and dimple the dough.
7. Bake 25-30 minutes, until golden.
8. Drizzle the vanilla icing over the warm focaccia and let rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

CINNAMON TOPPING
• 1 stick butter, browned
• 1 cup brown sugar
• 2 tbsp ground cinnamon
• 1 tsp vanilla

VANILLA ICING
• 1 cup powdered sugar
• enough heavy cream to thin it out
• 2 tsp vanilla extract

A FEW TIPS:
• The first fold will be GLOOPY. That’s normal, do your best.
• Wet your hands every time you do stretch and folds or coil folds to prevent sticking. 
• Don’t stretch until the dough breaks. Be gentle and stretch just until you feel tension.
• Once the dough gets bubbly, be gentle when transferring. Those bubbles are what we want!
• Don’t obsess over the clock when doing your final rest. Look for dough that has doubled, is jiggly and fullllllll of bubbles.
• This recipe is a plain focaccia recipe, feel free to add whatever toppings you like!

The smoothie itself was creamy and refreshing with sweet, chewy bits of sticky rice throughout.  Personally it had a bit of sourness and I wonder if the mango just wasn't ripe enough.  I definitely come back and give it another try.  And last but not least, Ullilani's mango sticky rice shaved ice.  Who knew mango sticky rice and shaved ice would work so well together?  The pillowy soft ice paired perfectly with a sweet mango puree and sticky rice, while the  ice cream on the bottom was almost like whipped ice cream, making it the perfect finish.

input.transcript: A mi familia no le gusta el sushi, pero en el cumpleaños de mi hermana,  preparé esta torta maqui y a todos les encantó.  Fas iniciar con una libra a roto de sushi que conseguís en cualquier supermercado.  Vas a lavarlo al menos 10 veces hasta que el agua salga clarita.  Lo preparás como dice las instrucciones del paquete y cuando esté listo lo llevas a una refractaria.  En una olla, gregas vinagre a roto.  A su carizal le tiras la mezcla de roto, distribuís muy bien y dejas enfriar.  En otro lado, un salmón le pone limón.  Salza de soya, se bollín.  Ajo de ingibrizal, buscas un recipiente y empezás a armar la torta.  Abajo una capa a roto, después del salmón, queso crema, páltey y le puse madoorito.  Terminamos con el arroz, damos vuelta con un plato, bañamos en una salsa sebichada,  se inilla damos un olí y listo.  Telen que hacerla.

input.caption: I am half boy half rotisserie chicken at this point #losangeles #foodvlog
input.transcript: These are all the best things I ate this month  as someone who works full-time in food media.  It's been so damn hot in LA recently.  So I ventured over to Malibu and went in Malibu,  you got a lilies.  Breakfast burritos are heavy on the refried beans.  I get it with Jody so, and it's perfect.  I'm also really into having soup when it's hot out.  So I figured it was a good time to try  Sawa Kaosoi in Studio City.  They give you all the fixin.  And that crispy chicken is so good  with the silky coconut milk broth.  I'm also taking this time to announce  that I am in my crawler era.  And it's all thanks to Nailetta,  a pop of cart making them hot and fresh.  They've got interesting glazes like chili cinnamon.  I like them playing.  I like to taste the egginess.  I also love this lamb shank from Roshona Bilal.  You've been golly stripped, Malibu.  Actually, I liked everything I had here.  This chicken rice, the paratha,  and the family members that run the spot are so chill,  so nice.  I love it here.  I also made this video for work  on three rotisserie chicken spots,  all in Pasadena.  The first spot was rotisserie chicken of California.  They do this tangy, vinegary, 32 spice blend.  The second spot was Sausage chicken.  They're doing interesting Indian Mexican fusion,  like this Injaro rotisserie chicken.  Also great sides, Antertya.  And the third spot was Loli Farms. input.transcript: If you love fried chicken, you need to know about this spot because it was voted one of the top places to eat in Orange County.  This is Bale Chicken Irvine and they have some seriously underrated fried chicken and Asian inspired comfort food.  Their popcorn chicken was so good and honestly the perfect little snack.  They have their own specialty oil and seasoning and trying the chicken with that added so much flavor.  I would definitely get this again on the go just so I could snack on it.  Then we had to try their famous original chicken sandwich and when I say this thing was huge, it was huge.  It was so juicy, crispy and packed with flavor. Some of the juiceiest chicken ever.  We also got their grilled bow with pork and let me just say this was probably my favorite thing that I had.  These were basically crispy, pan fried little pockets of goodness.  The crispy outside with that filling was so good.  These were some of the best grab and go bites I've ever had.  I even tried it with their special oil and seasoning and chef's kiss.  Then we got their beef soup which had tender beef potatoes and the super flavor were brought.  This was so homey and comforting and honestly tasted like a home cooked meal which I loved.  And of course we couldn't leave without trying more fried chicken.  We got their crispy wings and honey mustard wings and both were spectacular.  The chicken was crispy, juicy and perfectly seasoned.  So if you're in Irvine and love fried chicken, bow chicken definitely needs to be on your list.

input.caption:
Noriko in River West Chicago is an intimate handroll bar where every roll is made right in front of you.

😋 What I ordered:
* Puncha Matcha
* Lychee Martini
* Nori Chips & Dip
* Modern Handroll Set
* Spicy Octopus
* Yellowtail
* Bluefin Tuna Toro
* Bluefin Tuna Akami
* California
* Bay Scallop Dynamite
💵: $270

💭 Thoughts: The basement space has only 21 chef’s counter seats, dim moody lighting, and good music that isn’t too loud. You can watch the chefs make each handroll, making it a nice intimate dinner spot. 8.5/10.

Service was good overall. Everyone remembered our celebration and they surprised us with a card and complimentary prosecco, which was delicious. I also liked being seated at the end of the counter. My only issue was that we weren’t given ginger, wasabi, or soy sauce while other tables were, so I’m not sure if we were supposed to ask. 7/10.

The Nori Chips & Dip (8/10) had slightly oily nori, but the edamame hummus and chili crunch dip had a creamy texture with a nice little kick.

The Lychee Martini (7/10) was pretty standard. The Puncha Matcha (8/10) was more cucumber-forward than matcha, refreshing and very easy to drink.

The Toro (9/10) practically melted in my mouth, and the caviar added a nice pop of texture. The California (8/10) was surprisingly good with a nice balance of creamy avocado and crunchy cucumber. The Crab Motoyaki (8.5/10) was addicting with tender crab and a rich, savory topping.

The A5 Wagyu (6.5/10) was disappointing. I didn’t get much of the Wagyu flavor, and the crab cake and mayo sauce actually overpowered it. The Spicy Octopus (8/10) was one of my favorites with a nice chew and a good kick.

Everything tasted fresh, but most of the handrolls were pretty standard in flavor. Overall 7/10 for the handrolls.

📍 401 N Milwaukee Ave, Chicago, IL 60642

#chicagogram #chicagolife #chicagofood #chicagorestaurants #chicago
input.transcript: This sandroll bar is hidden under Perilla, and you can see the chefs make every roll in front of it.  I started with crispy nori chips with the creamy edamame hummus that had a little kick from the chili.  The canoria was slightly oily.  When Macha cocktail was super refreshing and the toro with kaffir was my favorite.  The fish practically melted in my mouth with low pops of kaffir.  The A-F-Iwagi was pretty disappointing because the crab peag-on top completely overpowered the meat.  The Maduro Yaqui was much better with the sweet, soy, and rich baked crab that was seriously addictive.  Most of the other rolls were pretty standard, but overall it was a fun one-time experience.

input.caption:
Gilt Bar in River North Chicago is a Michelin recognized American restaurant and bar known for its moody atmosphere and strong cocktail program.

😋 What I ordered: • Chocolate Martini • French Martini • Espresso Martini • Prosecco • Fried Chicken Sliders • Fried Onion Rings • Truffle Mafaldine • Steak & Ale Pot Pie • Prime Rib French Dip • Chocolate Layer Cake
💵: $210 + tip

💭 Thoughts: We joined the waitlist around 5:40 on Saturday and got seated within an hour. We ended up at a table near the entrance, so the atmosphere wasn’t quite as nice as the dining room. 7/10.

Service was top tier. 9.5/10. They genuinely cared about making things right when something went wrong. Our server even covered the forgotten Espresso Martini.

The Chocolate Martini (9.5/10) was creamy and chocolatey and dangerously easy to drink. The French Martini (9/10) was fruity and smooth. The Espresso Martini (7/10) was better than a lot I’ve tried but could’ve been foamier.

The Fried Chicken Sliders (8/10) were crispy, juicy, and perfectly coated in Nashville hot sauce without being drenched in sauce.

The Onion Rings (7/10) were crispy and oily with a nice spicy mayo.

The Truffle Mafaldine (8/10) was room temp, but the al dente pasta, creamy sauce, and truffle bits were heavenly.

The Steak & Ale Pot Pie (9/10) was fantastic. Tender brisket, flaky crispy puff pastry, and creamy mash underneath made it feel like short ribs and mash in pie form.

The Prime Rib French Dip (8.5/10) had tender, flavorful meat and au jus, but the bread was pretty plain.

The Chocolate Layer Cake (6/10) was a little dry and not quite chocolatey enough at first, but it got much better drenched in the hot fudge and paired with the vanilla gelato.

Overall, great time with amazing cocktails, top-tier service, and solid food.

✨ Recs: Chocolate Martini, Steak & Ale Pot Pie, Vanilla Gelato + Hot Fudge, French Martini, Prosecco

📍230 W Kinzie St, Chicago, IL 60654

input.transcript: LA's largest Korean food court is hidden inside this old mall.  It's actually K-town's first mall.  Behind us the oldest Korean food court too.  It looks frozen in time with old-school neon lights and classic Korean food stalls.  Here's everything to eat.  The most famous thing is the giant Korean style katsu.  The video doesn't even do it justice.  This plate is huge.  This cot looks bigger than my cot look.  I went here next because they had the longest line.  They're one of the oldest vendors known for beating up in a hot stone bowl.  I prefer my beating up unmixed but it makes it just for y'all.  It feels weird though.  Like eating a chapsala that wasn't chaps.  I like how Koreans always include sides and bon chan with their meals.  This dumpling house is also a long time vendor known for Korean style dumplings and these are the biggest dumplings ever.  So fluffy and stung.  My favorite Korean dish is jjajang man so I had to get that.  It was only 12 bucks for this big portion.  Then I got bulgogi from Plaza.  It's all known for home style Korean cooking and they include rice, bon chan and soup.  Not too much sugar in any of these vendors either.  Probably because they're so old.  Everything is so delicious here and the value for three hours of parking.  There's 10 vendors here currently so many more than I want to come back to try.  Clearly enough there's no dessert vendor in here though.  This mall is also home to the oldest Korean restaurant in the US.  That's a whole other shabang I'm going to come back for.  This is Korea Town Plaza Food Court.

input.caption:
trying to find the BEST food in California 🏃🏻‍♀️(ft. onion, onions, and more ONION 🧅)

📍first stop: The Kettle - 1138 Highland Ave, Manhattan Beach, CA 90266 

#fyp #eating #california #foodreels #foodreview where to eat
input.transcript: I'm trying to find the best food in California and it's only right to start in the most unlikely place Manhattan beat.  Where this unassuming kettle is actually a long standing diner that's been here for decades and has a look that's so cozy,  so let's start with the infamous buttermilk onion ring.  These are almost comically huge, you can't fully tell in the camera, but this felt like half an onion I'm about to eat.  Their ranch was insanely good, this is honestly a top three onion ring I've ever had and deserves a 10 out of 10.  You're gonna stand the onion theme and try their self-proclaimed best-in-the-state French onion soup.  I wasn't too excited for soup in this summer, but when in Cali, this was a very balanced and not overly salty French onion soup like others,  so this was pretty enjoyable. Let's take a break from onions because it actually doesn't stop there,  but now we're gonna move on to their barbecue pot roast quesadilla.  Definitely seems like a random choice, but I actually enjoyed this too, and it probably would be better as tacos instead of a quesadilla.  This had a nice smokiness and flavor to it, so this was pretty good.  You have another random choice, which is this corn carbonara, which I was told is new on the menu, and while I did enjoy this,  I don't know why I ordered this during lunchtime because it was giving dinner.  Creamy cheesiness was a bit overwhelming, but I did love that corn in there.  Those little parm bread pieces they had on the plate reminded me so much of old Chuck E Cheese Parmesan bread stick,  which was one of my favorite things, but before I could feel too torn up about it,  let's get back to some onions with this French onion burger.  This comes with melty Swiss cheese on a Parmesan crested brioche bun with caramelized onion jam,  a1 steak sauce, and their French onion soups.  You're probably wondering, what is up with all of these onions?  And to that, I say, no clue.  But when tasting this burger, it was a true meatloaf burger and the softness and flavor,  and thankfully, I enjoy meatloaf.  And again, paired with their French onion soup that is already good, this was interesting.  Overall, nothing was really bad.  Everything was pretty well made for a beach side restaurant.  So you won't feel like you wasted your money, but it won't be groundbreaking.  So the journey continues.  Let me know what your top pick is and where I should go to next.

This is the best new breakfast burrito in LA.  La Rue's is cute little food truck in LA,  and I went specifically on Sunday  for their Sunday only mama sando, but as a burrito.  It's filled with fluffy tomato eggs, bell peppers, onions,  cheese, crispy tater tots, green onions,  and avocado aioli.  I was in love after my first bite.  It was so flavorful, cheesy and rich.  I love the tomato eggs, and the tater tots  were perfectly crispy.  They actually cook everything in only butter and beef talo.  And he gave me a tater tot by itself to try,  and it was one of the best tater tots I've ever had.  I also got the fruity pebble matcha  and the pumpkin spy French toast with their homemade cream,  both were delicious.  And all their sauces, even the sriracha, is made in house.  I can't wait to come back.

i’d come back if i happened to be in the area, but if there’s a long wait, i probably wouldn’t go out of my way for it again 😂

input.transcript: This is one of my favorite Italian deli's near Tampa,  and now they're making sourdough for cacha sandwiches.  The family behind the shop grew up in New York.  They used their Italian known as recipes,  and brought that classic New York Italian deli experience to Tampa.  You walk in and the first thing you see is sweet,  it's pizza, a little Italian market, the deli section,  there's so much going on.  I got to Datsamore with homemade pesto,  garlic-infused olive oil, fresh mozzarella, tomato,  and you can add freshly sliced prosciutto.  Look at the size of this thing, it's massive.  And we also tried the Don Murtadella.  This one comes with freshly sliced Murtadella,  pistachio pesto, strascia tella, fresh pistachios.  Oh my god, this one was so good.  Like I'm telling you, it's amazing.  And the best part is that you can take basically any sandwich  on their menu and swap the regular bread further for cacha.  So we have to try the one with crispy chicken cutlets  and their homemade vodka sauce, and I'm telling you,  this bread with the vodka sauce is dangerous.  So yeah, when you walk in, all the desserts are literally staring at you.  It's a good luck saying no.  Their canollies are insane, and right now they even have a seasonal one  with pumpkin canolli cream, but the pistachio canolli is my favorite.  I just love this place, and you need to go.

input.transcript: This is the hardest inner reservation to get in LA and it's fully booked through the end of the year.  A little tip if you're visiting the Lucas Museum, put your name down as soon as you get in for a chance at Bar Seating.  The space is stunning and has these gorgeous handcrafted cherry wood panels,  and there's a gorgeous terrace with panoramic views of the city.  But now onto the food.  We started with the Bread Service, which pairs perfectly with the local honey butter, which comes from a cattle ranch nearby.  The Lucas Chop Salad is actually good with the juiciest local tomatoes. This is the Skywalker Grill at the Lucas Museum and Good Luck getting a reservation.

input.caption:
🚨 BRUNCH LOVERS, THIS ONE’S FOR YOU. 🚨

Late riser? Matcha addict? Or just someone who orders half the menu to share? 👀 Sip Sip’s Brunch Menu is calling your name! 😉

Here’s what went down at @sipsip.sg✨

🍯🍞 Cast Iron French Toast
Soft, pudding-like French toast served sizzling in a cast iron pan with butter, sea salt & maple syrup! Sweet, buttery and seriously comforting — basically brunch in it's best form 🥹💛

🥓🥖 Iberico Pork Jowl Flatbread
Grilled Iberico pork jowl + poached egg + garlicky labneh + sofrito + fresh herbs! The pork was rich and flavourful, while the creamy labneh and egg kept every bite balanced 🙌🏻 Definitely one to order! 💥

🥚🥔 Hasselback Potato
Triple-cooked for that irresistible crispy exterior, then loaded with hot honey, Dijon mustard, truffle egg salad, tobiko, gherkin & crispy bacon bits 🥰 Crispy, savoury, sweet, tangy… this was a flavour bomb 🔥

‼️🥦 Grilled Broccolini
Char-grilled, smoky and finished with brown butter & soy balsamic vinaigrette, plus toasted hazelnuts for crunch. A surprisingly addictive side that made vegetables feel VERY exciting 🙂‍↕️

🍓🍵 Matcha Strawberry — creamy matcha foam + strawberry compote + milk. Fruity, refreshing and nicely balanced 👏🏻

🍫🍰🍵 Tiramisu Matcha — matcha foam + milk + chocolate + tiramisu vibes. Richer and more indulgent, aka the one for dessert lovers 😉

💭 Verdict: Come hungry, order for the table and don’t skip the Hasselback Potato or Iberico Pork Jowl Flatbread! And make sure you save some room for their amazing matchas ☺️💚

input.caption:
Eggs, but make them seriously indulgent. 

Finally made it to @eggslut_portland, tucked inside Prost Marketplace. It’s a casual, lively food-cart-pod setting, so you get the energy of Mississippi Ave rather than a traditional brunch restaurant.

I tried two of their signature sandwiches: the Fairfax and the Sausage, Egg & Cheese. The Fairfax has soft scrambled eggs, cheddar, caramelized onions and sriracha mayo tucked into a warm brioche bun. Creamy, slightly spicy and probably the one I’d order again. The Sausage, Egg & Cheese is heartier, with chicken sausage, an over-medium egg, cheddar and honey mustard aioli.

And because breakfast apparently needed a little more decadence, we also had the fresh orange juice. It was a nice bright contrast to the rich sandwiches.

What I like about Eggslut is that they take something as simple as an egg sandwich and build a whole experience around it: soft eggs, buttery brioche, sauces, caramelized onions and plenty of savory flavors. If you’re a breakfast sandwich person, this is definitely one to add to your Portland list.

Next up is baby chon which is a Japanese inspired bakery and cafe.  My eyes immediately went to this matcha strawberry donut in their pastry case so I thought that. A colachies a traditional check pastry but I really need to come back here and make a full video on this to go more in-duck.  I got the blueberry one and I really liked it. input.transcript: Welcome to my New York City series where I'm eating the food from every city in China,  because I'm tired of people thinking that's the trend food is all that Chinese cuisine has to offer.  Today we're going to Yunnan in the southwest of China, and don't worry, I'll walk you through exactly  what's to order to maximize your meal. Yunnan is a mountainous region and known for five things.  Fregan herb forward flavors, edible rose, kirit mi, rice noodles, and wild mushrooms.  Your first going to order the tofu pudding rice noodles or dohua mi xiang.  These are the bounciest rice noodles topped with soft tofu,  braised pork, and pickled veggies, and yes, it existed before the viral Mapo tofu noodles.  This is a traditional dish local to the city of Kunming.  And because the fermented tofu sauce is so good, you have to get the fried tofu that comes with a  side of Yunnan style furu to dip. It's crispy on the outside, piping hot on the inside,  and the furu is packed with umami. You're also going to get the green papaya chicken soup with  Yunnan cured ham, or Yuntui, Sua Mojwati. Yunnan is known for freshness of our flavors, and this one  is exactly that. It's deeply flavorful, it has just the right amount of spice, and the chicken is very  tender. And since you obviously have to try something with rose, you're also going to end with the  sweet tofu pudding topped with rose, so silky, and refreshing, and not too sweet. Let me know what  city are the province of China you want to see next, and I will see you next week.

input.caption:
Is this the best fried chicken sandwich in Atlanta? 👀

@bombbiscuitatl in Grant Park has become one of Atlanta’s most celebrated breakfast spots, earning a Michelin Bib Gourmand and national recognition along the way.

I went with the hot honey fried chicken biscuit and added an egg over medium.

Buttery biscuit. Crispy fried chicken. Hot honey. Egg.

The biscuit is tender and rich. The chicken brings the crunch. Then the hot honey adds that sweet heat that makes the whole thing ridiculously easy to keep eating.

Chef and owner Erika Council built Bomb Biscuit around recipes and techniques passed down through her family. She learned biscuits through her grandmothers, including Mildred “Mama Dip” Council, and later turned that history into her own cookbook, Still We Rise.

Before Bomb Biscuit became a restaurant, Erika worked in tech and started cooking through pop-ups around Atlanta. One pop-up turned into more. Then came biscuit deliveries, breakfast collaborations, food stalls and eventually the full restaurant.

She’s since taken that biscuit story far beyond Atlanta through cookbook events, national food appearances and collaborations around the country.

And yes, the place was slammed when we got there.

Don’t let the line scare you. They move pretty quickly, and it’s absolutely worth the wait.

They’ve also got a full brunch lineup with cocktails, so this is not just a grab-a-biscuit-and-leave situation.

Come hungry.

#AtlantaEats #AtlantaFood #ATLFoodie #atlantafoodie #atleats

input.caption:
Fall dinner club ep. 6🍁
If you love French onion soup, you have to try this one!

If you want a printable version make sure you're following @home_with_hart comment PASTA and I'll send it to your DMs! 

French Onion Pasta
3 large yellow onions, thinly sliced 2 tbsp butter 1 tbsp olive oil
1 tsp balsamic glaze
3 cloves garlic, minced 1 tbsp fresh thyme ½ cup dry white wine 3 cups beef broth, plus more as needed 1–2 tsp Worcestershire sauce
1 lb long pasta (I used Mafaldine) ½ cup heavy cream 1½ cups shredded Gruyère Salt + pepper
Heat butter and olive oil in a large skillet. Add onions and a pinch of salt and cook over medium heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden and caramelized.
Add balsamic glaze, garlic and thyme and cook for another minute. Pour in the white wine and scrape up all those yummy browned bits. Let it reduce for 2–3 minutes.
Add Worcestershire and beef broth, then add the pasta directly to the skillet. Simmer, stirring frequently, until the pasta is al dente and the liquid has reduced into a sauce. Add a little more broth or water if needed.
Stir in the heavy cream, then reduce the heat and add the Gruyère a little at a time until melted and creamy. Season with salt and lots of black pepper.
Finish with fresh thyme and extra Gruyère and enjoy! 

#momof4 #easydinnerideas #fallcooking #frenchonion #pastarecipes
input.transcript: Welcome back to Fall Dinner Club.  This is episode six, and tonight I'm making French onion pasta.  This dish was everything I hoped it would be.  It's basically French onion soup turned into the coziest pasta dinner,  and I promise this one is worth a little bit of extra time.  It takes to caramelize those onions.  Guys, I'm telling you if you make this your house is going to smell amazing.  It's the perfect recipe for a cozy night in on a cold night.  I am bonus.  It all comes together in one pan.  You guys have to let me know if you try this one and tell me what you think about it.

input.caption:
MISO PANCETTA UDON 🍝

minimal prep + clean up = weeknight dinner made easy! 

ingredients —
+ 2 blocks udon
+ 4 oz. pancetta, diced
+ 1 cup brown mushrooms, sliced
+ 1 small shallot, chopped
+ 4 garlic cloves, minced
+ 2 Tbsp. white miso
+ ½ Tbsp. gochujang
+ ½ tsp. gochugaru
+ 2 whole eggs
+ 2 egg yolks
+ ½ cup parmesan, freshly grated
+ ½ tsp. black pepper, ground
+ 1 Tbsp. butter
+ chives, chopped

instructions —
1. Cook the udon according to package and reserve some pasta water on the side.
2. Start the pancetta in a cold skillet and cook over medium-low heat until crisp. Remove the pancetta, leaving the rendered fat behind.
3. Add the mushrooms, shallot, and garlic to the pan and sauté until softened.
4. Add the butter and udon, tossing everything together.
5. In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, yolks, miso, gochujang, gochugaru, parmesan, and black pepper.
6. Remove the skillet from the heat. Add the sauce mixture and mix constantly, then add the udon water 1 Tbsp. at a time until you get your desired sauce texture.
7. Fold in half of the crispy pancetta.
8. Finish with the remaining pancetta, parmesan and chives.

#udonnoodles #misopaste #pastarecipes #easymealideas #carbonara
input.transcript: This might be my new favorite way to eat udon. You've got crispy pancetta, brown mushrooms,  and this miso egg sauce that gets glossy once it hits the noodles. The sauce comes together  right in the pan so no heavy cream is needed. The miso gives it that savory dip. While the  gochujang adds just enough heat to keep you going back for another bite. Then you fold the  crispy pancetta back in, hit it with some chives, and extra parmesan, and that's it. The noodles  stay saucy, and this is just one of those recipes where you take one bite and immediately one another.

input.caption:
The best Beef Noodle Soup I’ve had in a while

📍Duan Chun Zhen
A Taiwanese beef noodle chain that landed in Perth with the beef noodle soup that kept me thinking about nonstop. The broth is simmered for hours with 23 herbs and spices, all imported from Taiwan to stay true to its roots.

They’re honestly one of the best I’ve had in Australia and I’m wishing I could have this in Melbourne 🥹 The broth was the winning factor for me with deep aromatic flavours that I cant seemed to get in Melbourne. The staff told me this is due to the hours of simmering and the quality of the beef. 

You can choose from 3 types of broth, customise your noodle thickness and meat cuts, and I highly recommend the mala broth which adds a bit of spice kick. Loved their sides too, especially the fried rice, pork chop and braised pork rice. Such an authentic spot!
Would definitely come back soon

They are famous for their homemade gimbab  which is one of my favorite.  Ugh, I must tell you.  There are Korean street toasts  is definitely one of the best.  Generous with ingredient  and the cheese pull is satisfying.  Enjoying the softiness from the pulled cheese  and the fragrant of cheese.  Nice.  Oh my god.  The soft pillowy of the bread  nice light toasted fragrant of butter  with the fluffy cloud egg and the sauce.  Instantly transport me to Isaac Toz and Wendor.  They are beef bibimbap to surprise me.  And you must add on this homemade sauce.  Then mix, mix, mix and stir well.  Enjoy this in a big bite like K-Drama.  Then you get explosion of flavors.  Beef is nicely marinated like bulgogi.  Heen of fresh sesame and a bite of cranniness from the veggies.  It's satisfying.  And their homemade kimchi is so good.  It's different from what I've tried.  Medium body in sauce.  Cut slightly smaller piece.  Spellance of sweetness and sourness.  I had three.  It's very rare to see variety of gimbap.  Puna is my favorite as it's with Perrilla leaf.  Perrilla dog gimbap is perfect for veggie de rind.  Spicy squid is both good to try.  And beef gimbap is one of their bests I love.  Oh, their mandu is so different.  Ingredients is well marinated.  It's with kimchi and chicken.  Korean fried rice won't go wrong with it.  And then with Korean hot dog.  Whenever I see this, it's a must try for me.  It is nicely pan-fried.  Nice light chewy dough with nice caramel brown sugar.  With cinnamon to my liking.  Give it a try.  If you are craving for Korean home street style food,  I would say can try here.
